scope: Pinned unchanged upstream FASM disassembly, format/parser and assembly; Rust semantic comparison and independent non-ECC positive-bit union. Static checks only.
checks: Exact tool profile byte identity binds all source/database/wheel identities before capture; source revision labels alone are insufficient.
Feature manifest tables, part and tilegrid must match the corresponding tool database objects.
Original non-ECC set is saved before the upstream disassembler mutates its data argument.
Every positive Rust predicate must occur in raw upstream names; unknown names and duplicates fail. Formatting may remove only zero-only defaults.
Parsed formatted names, formatted semantic digest/count, complete original/regenerated non-ECC sets and Rust asserted-bit union digest/count must agree.
Original checked frame map is reused with its known limitation: no second independent packet parser. ECC and missing-table records remain explicit.
Only captured inputs enter ordinary isolated execute; no KVM grant, network or host filesystem access is requested. Output truncation, nonzero exit and comparison failure remain failures.
Reviewed equivalent is_some_and form for canonical-name conflict detection after the initial source review. No semantic change.

Reviewed post-failure memory fix: hashes are computed before the heavy parse; completed disassembly tuples/data are released; unchanged assembler callback records the actual saved file parser semantics in its existing parse pass; completed frame/database intermediates are released before streamed JSON. All comparison assertions and the1GiB limit remain unchanged.

Reviewed bounded saved-text parser adapter after482b MemoryError, with whole-file textX allocation as the leading hypothesis. Pinned FasmFile grammar repeats independent FasmLine entries; formatter items containing CR/LF are explicitly rejected before writing, so multiline annotation semantics cannot cross a chunk boundary. Unchanged parser consumes complete <=256KiB line chunks, accumulated unchanged assembler errors remain fatal, and consumed-byte hash/size bind the complete saved text. A fixed155-byte fixture compares full meaningful parsed tuples including annotations/comments/ranges/zero values against whole parsing. All previous predicate and non-ECC bit-set assertions remain unchanged.
